name: vaccine adverse events overview
title: Vaccine adverse event decision chart: an event within 6 weeks of immunisation is reported whatever its cause; sort it into allergy to a component, a known reaction to the vaccine, a defective vaccine, a problem with how it was given, or coincidence, then decide whether the next dose is contraindicated, needs a precaution, or is left to public health

root.title: Event within 6 weeks of a vaccine: did the VACCINE cause it, and can the NEXT dose go ahead?
lines: EVERY adverse event following immunisation (AEFI) → AEFI form to the local Public Health Unit: MANDATORY for immunisers
PRECAUTIONS before any dose: moderate or severe acute illness · a LIVE vaccine when immunocompromised or pregnant

groups.title: The VACCINE, how it was MADE, or how it was GIVEN
NOT the vaccine
lines: after it in time, not caused by it

head: h
Allergy to a component
e.g. polyethylene glycol (PEG) in the Pfizer mRNA vaccine
pres: after MMR, tetanus, hepatitis B or mRNA vaccines
next: treat it now: see the ALLERGY chart

head: h
A known reaction to the vaccine
the event fits that vaccine type
pres: • whole-cell pertussis → prolonged crying, seizures, hypotonic hyporesponsive episode
• viral vector → vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT), Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS)
next: ABSOLUTE: encephalopathy after a pertussis vaccine
• extensive limb swelling or high fever after the last dose
• GBS within 6 weeks of a flu vaccine

head: h
A defective vaccine
a component made wrongly
pres: after oral polio vaccine that was not inactivated enough

head: h
How it was GIVEN
an error, or the patient's anxiety
pres: contaminated vial → abscess at the injection site

head: h
Coincidence
independent of the vaccine
pres: e.g. a fractured radius, a UTI

rows: Public health advises on the next dose
the medical officer of health (MOH) or public health nurse reviews the report
